Resolves #19413

The claim responder no longer counts a pull request inside a contributor's fork as a hold. `holders` now counts an open closing reference only when its base repository is this one, and the workflow passes each pull request's `repository { nameWithOwner }`. A pull request from a fork into this repository still counts, because its base is this repository.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms on `decideReply`, red on `dev`'s module) plus a live, read-only run of the workflow's new query → L2 required (the rule is a pure function; the workflow only fetches and posts). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline pr-body and the engine CI ran.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `claimResponse.spec` reproduces #19230's shape. Claimant `Saadanjum01` claims, and the only closing reference is a draft by `Saadanjum0` whose base is `Saadanjum0/neo`. The claimant is first in line, and the reply carries no `#1`. The arm fails against `dev`'s module. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the existing "taken" arm, now passing `repository: 'neomjs/neo'`, still names #19200. |
| AC-3 | Outside CI, since the workflow only runs on a live claim: the new query, run read-only against #19230, returns `repository.nameWithOwner` for each closing reference. Today that is #19412, a pull request from `Saadanjum0`'s fork into this repository, whose base reads `neomjs/neo`, so it would still count. |
